Stopped timers have completed sessions with populated stopped_at timestamps.

startedFrom.description:
ISO 8601 date-time lower bound for filtering timers started on or after this timestamp.

Specifies the earliest point-in-time for timer start dates. Supports range queries for recent or historical timer sessions when combined with startedTo. Example: "2024-03-01T00:00:00Z" returns timers started from March 1st onward. Omitting returns all timer start times.
startedFrom.x-autobe-specification: Query parameter: Range filter on started_at column. WHERE started_at >= startedFrom ISO 8601 date-time value. Optional lower bound; omitting removes minimum start time constraint. Combines with startedTo for range queries. Filters timers initiated on or after the specified timestamp for historical or recent session windows.

startedTo.description:
ISO 8601 date-time upper bound for filtering timers started on or before this timestamp.

Specifies the latest point-in-time for timer start dates. Supports range queries for specific historical periods or recent time windows when combined with startedFrom. Example: "2024-03-31T23:59:59Z" returns timers started up to March 31st. Omitting returns all timer start times without upper limit.
startedTo.x-autobe-specification: Query parameter: Range filter on started_at column. WHERE started_at <= startedTo ISO 8601 date-time value. Optional upper bound; omitting removes maximum start time constraint. Combines with startedFrom for date-range queries. Filters timers initiated on or before the specified timestamp for historical period scoping.

cursor.description:
Opaque pagination cursor token for continuing a previous query result set.

Enables cursor-based (keyset) pagination for efficient large dataset navigation without page number math. Provide the cursor string value from a previous page response's pagination cursor field. Server decodes and resumes the query from that position. Alternative to page-based pagination (page/limit parameters). Omitting returns the first page of results.
cursor.x-autobe-specification: Query parameter: Server-side pagination continuation token. Implements cursor-based keyset pagination on hrm_platform_timers for efficient ordered result set navigation. Opaque string token; client receives from previous page response's pagination.cursor field, then provides to next request. Server decodes cursor token to resume query from the last returned record position. Alternative to page-based pagination; use either cursor OR page-based pagination (limit/page). Omitting returns first page via default pagination.

limit.description:
Number of timer records to return per page, ranging from 1 to 100.

Controls pagination result set size for both cursor-based and page-based queries. Defaults to system-defined page size if omitted. Maximum of 100 prevents excessive result set queries. Applied after all filtering and organization scoping constraints.
limit.x-autobe-specification: Query parameter: Pagination LIMIT clause for SQL result set. Valid range 1–100 records per page. Validates minimum 1 (rejects zero/negative) and maximum 100 (rejects excessive queries). Optional; defaults to system-defined page size if omitted. Controls result set size for both cursor-based and page-based pagination modes. Applied after all filters and organization scope enforcement. WHERE conditions + LIMIT clause in SQL query construction.

page.description:
1-indexed page number for page-based timer result navigation.

Specifies which page of results to retrieve using page-based pagination (OFFSET calculation). Starts at 1 for the first page. Combined with limit parameter for page size. Alternative to cursor-based pagination (cursor parameter). Defaults to page 1 if omitted. Requesting pages beyond available result range returns empty data array with pagination metadata reflecting actual total pages and records.
page.x-autobe-specification: Query parameter: 1-indexed page number for page-based OFFSET pagination. Calculates OFFSET = (page - 1) * limit. Page 1 = OFFSET 0. Combined with limit parameter for page navigation. Alternative to cursor-based pagination. Optional; defaults to page 1 if omitted. Exceeding available pages returns empty data array with valid pagination metadata.

IHrmPlatformTimer.IRequest.description:
Search and filter timer tracking sessions within the authenticated member's active organization.

Request supports full-text description search, entity ownership scoping (employee, project, task), timer activity status (running vs stopped), and start time range boundaries. Two pagination modes supported: cursor-based continuation with opaque cursor tokens, or page-based with explicit page numbers. All parameters are optional.

### Search & Filters
- `search`: Full-text matching against timer descriptions
- `employeeId`: Scope to specific employee's timers by UUID
- `projectId`: Scope to specific project timers by UUID
- `taskId`: Scope to specific task timers by UUID (nullable per timer)
- `active`: Boolean filter — true returns running timers (stopped_at IS NULL), false returns stopped timers
- `startedFrom`: ISO 8601 lower bound for started_at range
- `startedTo`: ISO 8601 upper bound for started_at range

### Pagination
- `cursor`: Opaque continuation token from previous page response
- `limit`: Result set size per page (1–100, defaults to system page size)
- `page`: 1-indexed page number for page-based pagination (defaults to 1)
IHrmPlatformTimer.IRequest.x-autobe-specification: Request body schema for PATCH /hrmPlatform/member/timers search/list operation. Filters timer tracking sessions via query parameters: full-text description search, entity FK filters (employeeId→hrm_platform_employees_id, projectId→hrm_platform_projects_id, taskId→hrm_platform_tasks_id), boolean active status from stopped_at IS NULL, date-time range on started_at (startedFrom/startedTo), and pagination via opaque cursor token with limit/page. Authenticated member scope enforced via JWT session — hrm_platform_members_id injected server-side. All parameters optional; omitting returns default paginated results. Organization context scoping applied via session middleware on hrm_platform_organizations via hrm_platform_members → employee → organization relationship chain.

employee.description:
Employee identity associated with the grouped time data.

Contains the employee summary when the report is grouped by employee dimension, including display name, role, department, employment type, and status. When grouped by project or task, this field may show the primary employee context or be null if the context is not applicable.
employee.x-autobe-specification: Computed via LEFT JOIN from hrm_platform_timelogs.hrm_platform_employee_id to hrm_platform_employees.id. When the grouping dimension is 'employee', this always contains the IHrmPlatformEmployee.ISummary for the grouped employee. When the grouping dimension is 'project' or 'task', this field reflects the primary employee context from the timelogs in that group and may be null if no employee context is available in the aggregation result. Returns IHrmPlatformEmployee.ISummary type.

project.description:
Project context associated with the grouped time data.

Contains the project summary when the report is grouped by project dimension, including project name, color code, status, budget, and timeline information. When grouped by employee or task, this field may show the project context or be null if the context is not directly applicable.
project.x-autobe-specification: Computed via LEFT JOIN from hrm_platform_timelogs.hrm_platform_project_id to hrm_platform_projects.id. When the grouping dimension is 'project', this always contains the IHrmPlatformProject.ISummary for the grouped project. When the grouping dimension is 'employee' or 'task', this field reflects the project context from the timelogs in that group and may be null if no project context is available. Returns IHrmPlatformProject.ISummary type.

task.description:
Task context associated with the grouped time data.

Contains the task summary when the report is grouped by task dimension, including task title, status, priority, estimated hours, and due date. When grouped by employee or project, this field is typically null as task-level detail is not the primary grouping context.
task.x-autobe-specification: Computed via LEFT JOIN from hrm_platform_timelogs.hrm_platform_task_id to hrm_platform_tasks.id. When the grouping dimension is 'task', this always contains the IHrmPlatformTask.ISummary for the grouped task. When the grouping dimension is 'employee' or 'project', this field may be null as task detail is not the primary grouping context. Returns IHrmPlatformTask.ISummary type.

total_hours.description:
Total hours worked, including both billable and non-billable time.

Sum of all logged time entries for this group expressed in decimal hours. Computed by aggregating duration_minutes from matching timelogs and dividing by 60.
total_hours.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation: SUM(duration_minutes) / 60 from hrm_platform_timelogs within the filter criteria and grouping dimension. Sums all duration_minutes values for all timelogs matching the date range, organization, and optional filters, then divides by 60 to convert from minutes to decimal hours. Always non-negative. Number type.

billable_hours.description:
Billable hours representing time chargeable to clients.

Sum of all logged time entries marked as billable for this group, expressed in decimal hours. Used for client invoicing and revenue tracking calculations.
billable_hours.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation: SUM(CASE WHEN billable THEN duration_minutes ELSE 0 END) / 60 from hrm_platform_timelogs within the filter criteria and grouping dimension. Only sums duration_minutes where the billable column is true. Divides by 60 to convert from minutes to decimal hours. Always non-negative. Number type.

non_billable_hours.description:
Non-billable hours representing internal or overhead work time.

Sum of all logged time entries marked as non-billable for this group, expressed in decimal hours. Used for cost tracking and internal utilization analysis.
non_billable_hours.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation: SUM(CASE WHEN NOT billable THEN duration_minutes ELSE 0 END) / 60 from hrm_platform_timelogs within the filter criteria and grouping dimension. Only sums duration_minutes where the billable column is false. Divides by 60 to convert from minutes to decimal hours. Always non-negative. Number type.

IReportTime.description:
Aggregated time tracking report entry containing computed hourly statistics and entity context.

Represents a single grouped row in the time tracking report results. Each entry corresponds to one group key determined by the requested grouping dimension (employee, project, or task) and contains the total hours, billable hours, and non-billable hours for that group. Entity context fields provide identity information such as the employee who performed the work, the project being tracked, or the specific task being worked on.
IReportTime.x-autobe-specification:
Computed aggregation schema derived from hrm_platform_timelogs with LEFT JOINs to entity reference tables.

Query pattern:
- Aggregates hrm_platform_timelogs filtered by date range (from, to), organization context, and optional filters (employee_id, project_id, task_id, billable)
- LEFT JOIN to hrm_platform_employees via hrm_platform_employee_id for employee entity context
- LEFT JOIN to hrm_platform_projects via hrm_platform_project_id for project entity context
- LEFT JOIN to hrm_platform_tasks via hrm_platform_task_id for task entity context
- GROUP BY the specified grouping dimension: employee_id, project_id, or task_id

Calculations:
- total_hours = SUM(duration_minutes) / 60
- billable_hours = SUM(CASE WHEN billable THEN duration_minutes ELSE 0 END) / 60
- non_billable_hours = SUM(CASE WHEN NOT billable THEN duration_minutes ELSE 0 END) / 60

Entity context fields (employee, project, task) are populated based on the requested grouping dimension. The primary grouping entity is always populated; secondary entities may be null depending on the dimension.

Authorization: member actor scoped to current organization via middleware. Managers/owners can view all employees' timelogs. Employees without time:manage permission are filtered to their own hrm_platform_employee_id only.

hoursToday.description:
Sum of hours worked today.

Aggregated value calculated from the sum of all timelog durations for the current calendar date, converted from minutes to hours by dividing by 60. Returns 0 when no timelogs exist for today.
hoursToday.x-autobe-specification: Computation logic: SELECT SUM(duration_minutes)/60 FROM hrm_platform_timelogs WHERE hrm_platform_employee_id = employeeId AND date >= start_of_today() AND date < start_of_tomorrow() AND deleted_at IS NULL. Returns 0 when NULL (no matching timelogs). Query is scoped to the employee's organization context.

hoursThisWeek.description:
Sum of hours worked this week.

Aggregated value calculated from the sum of all timelog durations for the current week period (Monday through Sunday), converted from minutes to hours by dividing by 60. Returns 0 when no timelogs exist for the current week.
hoursThisWeek.x-autobe-specification: Computation logic: SELECT SUM(duration_minutes)/60 FROM hrm_platform_timelogs WHERE hrm_platform_employee_id = employeeId AND date >= start_of_monday() AND date < start_of_next_monday() AND deleted_at IS NULL. Returns 0 when NULL (no matching timelogs). Query uses Monday-to-Sunday week convention.

activeTimer.description:
Currently active timer session if one exists.

Represents the active real-time tracking session for the authenticated employee's ongoing work. Includes the project and optional task the timer is tracking. Returns null when no timer is currently running for this employee.

The active status is determined by whether stopped_at is null.
activeTimer.x-autobe-specification: Computation logic: SELECT from hrm_platform_timers WHERE hrm_platform_employees_id = employeeId AND stopped_at IS NULL AND deleted_at IS NULL. At most one record per employee. Joins with hrm_platform_projects for project name, hrm_platform_tasks for task title. Returns the timer summary object, or null if no active timer exists.

recentTimelogs.description:
The five most recent timelog entries.

Array of time tracking records representing the most recent work periods logged by the employee, ordered by creation time (most recent first). Each entry includes project context, task details (if tracked), work description, and billable status.

Limited to the 5 most recent entries for display efficiency.
recentTimelogs.x-autobe-specification: Computation logic: SELECT TOP 5 from hrm_platform_timelogs WHERE hrm_platform_employee_id = employeeId AND deleted_at IS NULL ORDER BY created_at DESC. Joins with hrm_platform_projects for project name and hrm_platform_tasks for task title. Returns array of up to 5 most recent timelog entries based on creation order.

pendingTimesheet.description:
Any draft or submitted timesheet awaiting approval.

Represents the most recent timesheet that is either in draft status (being prepared by the employee) or submitted status (awaiting manager review). Returns null when no timesheets require attention.

Timesheets track weekly work (Monday-Sunday) and support workflow states: draft, submitted, approved, rejected.
pendingTimesheet.x-autobe-specification: Computation logic: SELECT from hrm_platform_timesheets WHERE hrm_platform_employee_id = employeeId AND status IN ('draft','submitted') AND deleted_at IS NULL. Returns the most recent pending timesheet (most recently updated) or null if no pending timesheets exist.

assignedTasks.description:
Open and in-progress task assignments.

Array of work items assigned to the employee that are either in open status (awaiting to be worked on) or in-progress status (currently being worked on). Limited to 5 tasks for dashboard display.

Each task includes project context for tracking scope.
assignedTasks.x-autobe-specification: Computation logic: SELECT from hrm_platform_tasks WHERE hrm_platform_employee_id = employeeId AND status IN ('open','in-progress') AND deleted_at IS NULL LIMIT 5. Joins with hrm_platform_projects for project name. Returns array of up to 5 tasks that are open or in-progress.

IPersonalDashboardView.description:
Personal dashboard view summarizing workforce metrics for the currently authenticated member within their active organization context.

Aggregated hours include today's tracked hours and this week's tracked hours, both calculated from timelog durations. The active timer field shows the currently running timer session if one exists. Recent timelog entries display the five most recent time records. The pending timesheet indicates any draft or submitted timesheet awaiting approval. Assigned tasks list open and in-progress work items.
IPersonalDashboardView.x-autobe-specification: Computed/aggregated dashboard view providing workforce metrics for the authenticated member's employee record within their active organization context. Queries multiple tables with organization scope enforcement: 1) hoursToday: SELECT SUM(duration_minutes)/60 FROM hrm_platform_timelogs WHERE hrm_platform_employee_id = employeeId AND date >= start_of_today() AND date < start_of_tomorrow() AND deleted_at IS NULL (returns 0 on NULL). 2) hoursThisWeek: SELECT SUM(duration_minutes)/60 FROM hrm_platform_timelogs WHERE hrm_platform_employee_id = employeeId AND date >= start_of_monday() AND date < start_of_next_monday() AND deleted_at IS NULL (returns 0 on NULL). 3) activeTimer: SELECT from hrm_platform_timers WHERE hrm_platform_employees_id = employeeId AND stopped_at IS NULL AND deleted_at IS NULL - joins hrm_platform_projects (project), hrm_platform_tasks (task optional), returns single timer or null. 4) recentTimelogs: SELECT TOP 5 from hrm_platform_timelogs WHERE hrm_platform_employee_id = employeeId AND deleted_at IS NULL ORDER BY created_at DESC - joins hrm_platform_projects, hrm_platform_tasks. 5) pendingTimesheet: SELECT from hrm_platform_timesheets WHERE hrm_platform_employee_id = employeeId AND status IN ('draft','submitted') AND deleted_at IS NULL - returns most recent pending timesheet or null. 6) assignedTasks: SELECT from hrm_platform_tasks WHERE hrm_platform_employee_id = employeeId AND status IN ('open','in-progress') AND deleted_at IS NULL LIMIT 5 - joins hrm_platform_projects. All queries verify hrm_platform_organization_id matches session organization.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the timer tracking session.

This UUID uniquely identifies the timer record throughout its entire lifecycle from creation to stopping or discarding.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_platform_timers.id. Primary key, UUID type. Auto-generated by the database upon timer creation.

member.description:
The authenticated member who initiated this timer session.

Members represent global user identities shared across all organization contexts. This field identifies which member account owns the timer and is resolved from the authenticated session. Used for audit and tracking purposes.
member.x-autobe-specification: BELONGS-TO relation join via hrm_platform_members_id → hrm_platform_members.id. Returns IHrmPlatformMember.ISummary containing the authenticated member's profile information (id, email, display_name, avatar_image, phone_number, created_at).

employee.description:
The employee actively timing work for the associated project.

Each timer belongs to exactly one employee who is assigned to the project through an active project membership. The employee must have active status to start and manage timers.
employee.x-autobe-specification: BELONGS-TO relation join via hrm_platform_employees_id → hrm_platform_employees.id. Returns IHrmPlatformEmployee.ISummary containing employee-specific information (member, role, department, position, employment_type, status, created_at) within the current organization context.

project.description:
The project against which time is being accumulated.

Time tracking is always scoped to a specific project within the organization. The project must have Active status and the employee must have an active project membership for it.
project.x-autobe-specification: BELONGS-TO relation join via hrm_platform_projects_id → hrm_platform_projects.id. Returns IHrmPlatformProject.ISummary containing project details (id, name, color_code, status, budget, start_date, end_date, created_at, updated_at, organization). Project must be in Active status to accept time tracking.

task.description:
The optional task for granular work item time tracking.

When provided, the task must belong to the associated project. Allows detailed time attribution to specific work items within the broader project scope. Null when time is tracked against the project without task-level attribution.
task.x-autobe-specification: BELONGS-TO relation join via hrm_platform_tasks_id (nullable) → hrm_platform_tasks.id. Returns IHrmPlatformTask.ISummary or null. When provided, the task must belong to the associated project. Uses oneOf schema for nullable handling.

description.description:
Optional user-provided description of the work being tracked during this session.

Provides context for the time effort. Nullable - null indicates no description was provided by the user. This description can be updated while the timer is running.
description.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_platform_timers.description. Nullable string column. User-provided context for the tracked work. When the timer stops and converts to a timelog, this description may be carried over to the timelog entry.

billable.description:
Flag indicating whether the tracked time should be classified as billable work.

When true, the hours count toward billable time tracking and client billing. When false, time is recorded as internal or non-billable effort.
billable.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_platform_timers.billable. Boolean column. When the timer stops and a timelog is created, this flag is transferred to the resulting timelog entry. Defaults to true if not explicitly specified by the user during timer creation.

started_at.description:
Timestamp recording when the tracking session was initiated.

Set automatically when the timer starts. This timestamp marks the beginning of the work tracking period and is used to calculate elapsed time when combined with the stop timestamp.
started_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_platform_timers.started_at. DateTime column. Set automatically to the current timestamp when the timer is created. Immutable - this value does not change after creation. Used with stopped_at to calculate total tracked duration.

stopped_at.description:
Timestamp recording when the tracking session was stopped.

Null while the timer is actively running. Once populated, the timer has been stopped and a corresponding timelog entry has been automatically created from the accumulated duration.
stopped_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_platform_timers.stopped_at. Nullable DateTime column. Null while the timer is actively running. Populated when the user stops the timer, triggering creation of a final timelog entry. Duration is calculated as stopped_at minus started_at, rounded to the nearest minute. Uses oneOf schema for nullable handling.

created_at.description:
System-managed timestamp of when this timer record was initially created in the database.

Automatically set upon record insertion. This value is immutable and does not change regardless of subsequent timer updates or state transitions.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_platform_timers.created_at. DateTime column. System-managed creation timestamp set automatically when the timer record is inserted. Immutable - does not change throughout the timer's lifecycle.

updated_at.description:
System-managed timestamp of when this timer record was last modified.

Updated automatically whenever any field on the timer is changed, such as during updates to the description, project assignment, task assignment, or billable status while the timer is running.
updated_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_platform_timers.updated_at. DateTime column. System-managed update timestamp updated automatically on every field modification. Changed when timer attributes (description, project, task, billable) are updated via the PATCH/PUT endpoint.

deleted_at.description:
Timestamp of when this timer was discarded via soft-deletion.

Null when the timer is active or was normally stopped with a timelog created. Populated when the user discards the timer session, removing it without generating any time tracking record. Discarded timers can still be retrieved for audit history.
deleted_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_platform_timers.deleted_at. Nullable DateTime column. Null when the timer is active or normally stopped. Populated with a timestamp when the timer is discarded (soft-deleted) without generating a timelog entry. Uses oneOf schema for nullable handling.

IHrmPlatformTimer.description:
Full details of a timer tracking session for real-time work effort tracking against a project with optional task assignment.

A timer represents an active or completed work tracking clock initiated by an employee within their organization context. Timers accumulate time against the associated project and can optionally attribute time to a specific task for granular tracking. When stopped, the accumulated duration is automatically converted into a timelog entry. Discarded timers are soft-deleted without generating any timelog.

Key aspects:

- **Ownership**: Each timer is linked to the authenticated member and their active employee record within the current organization.
- **Tracking scope**: Time is always tracked against a project, and can optionally be attributed to a task within that project.
- **Lifecycle**: Active timers have null stopped_at. Stopped timers have both started_at and stopped_at populated and generate a timelog. Discarded timers have deleted_at populated and generate no timelog.
- **Billability**: The billable flag determines whether tracked hours count as billable or internal work.
IHrmPlatformTimer.x-autobe-specification:
Direct mapping from hrm_platform_timers table with BELONGS-TO relation joins.

Direct columns: id, description (nullable), billable, started_at, stopped_at (nullable), created_at, updated_at, deleted_at (nullable).

BELONGS-TO relations:
- member: hrm_platform_members_id → IHrmPlatformMember.ISummary via $ref
- employee: hrm_platform_employees_id → IHrmPlatformEmployee.ISummary via $ref
- project: hrm_platform_projects_id → IHrmPlatformProject.ISummary via $ref
- task: hrm_platform_tasks_id → IHrmPlatformTask.ISummary|null via $ref/oneOf (nullable FK)

No HAS-MANY compositions. Timer is a leaf/terminal record in the domain.

Nullable DB fields use oneOf pattern: description (String?), stopped_at (DateTime?), deleted_at (DateTime?), task (FK?).

IHrmPlatformActivityLog.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_platform_activity_logs table. Relations: organization via JOIN on hrm_platform_organization_id (transformed to $ref IHrmPlatformOrganization.ISummary), member via JOIN on hrm_platform_member_id (transformed to $ref IHrmPlatformMember.ISummary). HAS-MANY composition: activityLogDetails from hrm_platform_activity_log_details joined on hrm_platform_activity_log_id. FK scalars removed. entityName nullable (oneOf). CamelCase property names: action_type→actionType, entity_type→entityType, entity_id→entityId, entity_name→entityName, created_at→createdAt.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the project membership record.

Used for identifying the specific assignment to perform updates, deletions, or fetch details.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from `hrm_platform_project_memberships.id`. Primary key UUID.

capacity_role.description:
The role assigned to the employee within this project.

Values are `member` (view tasks, log time) or `project-lead` (manage tasks, assign work). Determines the task-related permissions for this assignment.

employee.description:
The employee assigned to this project.

Contains summary details of the employee including their linked member profile, role, and department.
employee.x-autobe-specification: Transformed from `hrm_platform_employee_id`. Joins to `hrm_platform_employees` and returns `IHrmPlatformEmployee.ISummary`.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the employee was assigned to the project.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from `hrm_platform_project_memberships.created_at`. Format: ISO 8601 date-time.

IHrmPlatformProjectMembership.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a project membership that links an employee to a project with a specific capacity role.

Includes the membership UUID, the assigned capacity role (`member` or `project-lead`) which determines task management permissions, the employee reference, and the creation timestamp. Excludes heavy project details and metadata timestamps to optimize list payloads.
IHrmPlatformProjectMembership.ISummary.x-autobe-specification:
Direct mapping from `hrm_platform_project_memberships` database table.

Included columns: `id`, `capacity_role`, `created_at`.
Included relation: `employee` (transformed to `IHrmPlatformEmployee.ISummary` via FK `hrm_platform_employee_id`).

Excluded fields: `updated_at`, `deleted_at` (Summary DTO optimization), `hrm_platform_project_id`, `project` (Project context is implied by the API endpoint path).

projectId.description: The unique identifier of the project for which this budget utilization report is generated. This UUID matches the projectId used in the request path parameter, confirming which project the report applies to and enabling direct correlation with other project-specific endpoints.
projectId.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_platform_projects.id. Returned as a UUID-formatted string for identification and API path parameter correlation.

projectName.description: The name of the project as configured within the organization. Provides human-readable project identification in reports and dashboards, avoiding the need for additional database lookups when displaying budget utilization summaries.
projectName.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_platform_projects.name. Returned as a plain string for display purposes in UI components and reports.

budgetHours.description: The total configured budget hours for the project, or null if no budget has been set for this project. This value represents the planned time allocation in hours. When null, the project operates without a predefined budget constraint, and percentageConsumed will also be null regardless of actual logged hours.
budgetHours.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_platform_projects.budget (Float?, nullable). Returns the configured budget hours value or null if the project has no budget set. No transformation applied; value is passed through as-is.

actualHours.description: The total number of actual hours logged against this project, derived from all non-deleted timelog entries. Calculated by summing the duration_minutes from every timelog linked to this project and dividing by 60 to produce hours. Only timelogs that have not been soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NULL) are included. This value increases over time as team members log work against the project.
actualHours.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation from hrm_platform_timelogs via the timelogs relation on hrm_platform_projects. SUM(duration_minutes) WHERE hrm_platform_project_id = projectId AND deleted_at IS NULL, then divided by 60 to convert minutes to hours. Includes all timelogs regardless of billable status or timesheet association. Returns 0.0 if no matching non-deleted timelogs exist.

percentageConsumed.description: The percentage of the project budget that has been consumed by actual logged hours. Calculated as (actualHours / budgetHours) * 100. A value of 100 indicates the project has consumed its entire budget; values above 100 indicate a budget overrun. Returns null when the project has no configured budget or a zero budget, since division is not possible.
percentageConsumed.x-autobe-specification: Computed as (actualHours / budgetHours) * 100 when budgetHours is greater than zero. Returns null when budgetHours is null or zero. No rounding applied; returns the raw floating-point result to preserve precision for downstream calculations.

IBudgetUtilization.description:
Budget utilization report for a single project.

Returned by the GET /hrmPlatform/member/projects/{projectId}/reports/utilization endpoint. Provides a snapshot comparing the project's configured budget hours against the actual hours consumed from all timelog entries, along with a computed percentage indicating budget consumption.

This DTO serves project managers and organizational administrators monitoring resource allocation and budget compliance. If a project has no budget configured, budgetHours and percentageConsumed will be null, while actualHours will still reflect total logged time.
IBudgetUtilization.x-autobe-specification:
Aggregation DTO primarily sourced from hrm_platform_projects with timelogs aggregation via the timelogs relation.

Direct mappings:
- projectId: hrm_platform_projects.id
- projectName: hrm_platform_projects.name
- budgetHours: hrm_platform_projects.budget (Float?, nullable)

Computed aggregations:
- actualHours: SUM(hrm_platform_timelogs.duration_minutes) WHERE hrm_platform_project_id = projectId AND deleted_at IS NULL, divided by 60 to convert minutes to hours. Returns 0.0 if no matching timelogs exist.
- percentageConsumed: (actualHours / budgetHours) * 100 when budgetHours > 0. Null when budgetHours is null or zero.

Filtering: Only non-deleted timelogs included (deleted_at IS NULL). All timelogs counted regardless of billable status or timesheet association.

employee_breakdowns.description:

IHrmPlatformProjectBudgetReport.description:
Comprehensive budget utilization report for a project. Displays the project's core attributes (id, name, color_code, status, dates) alongside calculated time tracking statistics. Aggregates all valid timelogs to compute total actual hours logged, the percentage of the planned budget consumed, structured breakdowns of time contributions by individual employees, and the separation of billable client time versus internal organizational work.

Utilization metrics are null if the project has no budget set, and actual hours default to 0 if no timelogs exist.
IHrmPlatformProjectBudgetReport.x-autobe-specification: Aggregated budget utilization report. Filters hrm_platform_projects and hrm_platform_timelogs (timelogs.hrm_platform_project_id = projectId). actual_hours = SUM(timelogs.duration_minutes) / 60.0 for timelogs.deleted_at IS NULL. utilization_percent = (actual_hours / budget) * 100.0 (or null if budget is null). employee_breakdowns = GROUP BY timelogs.hrm_platform_employee_id aggregating duration_minutes and COUNT(*). billable_breakdowns = GROUP BY timelogs.billable aggregating duration_minutes and COUNT(*) per employee. Includes direct project properties: id, name, color_code, budget, status, start_date, end_date, created_at, updated_at. Returns 404 if project not found or outside scope.

activeEmployeesCount.description:
Total number of active employees within the organization.

This metric represents the headcount of employees currently with an active status, providing an overview of the organization's current workforce size. Only employees with status 'active' are counted, excluding deactivated or terminated employees.
activeEmployeesCount.x-autobe-specification: COUNT query from hrm_platform_employees table filtered by status='active' and organization_id matching the session context. Returns an integer representing the total count of active employees.

totalHoursThisWeek.description:
Total hours logged this week across the organization.

This metric represents the sum of all time tracking entries within the current calendar week (Monday to Sunday). The value is calculated by summing duration_minutes from timelogs and dividing by 60 to convert to hours.
totalHoursThisWeek.x-autobe-specification: SUM query from hrm_platform_timelogs table filtered by date within current week (Monday to Sunday relative to current system date), organization_id matching session context via employee relationship. Sum duration_minutes and divide by 60 to get total hours as a number.

pendingTimesheetsCount.description:
Count of pending timesheets awaiting approval.

This metric represents the number of timesheets that have been submitted by employees but have not yet been approved or rejected. Provides managers with visibility into the review workload and helps track the timesheet submission lifecycle.
pendingTimesheetsCount.x-autobe-specification: COUNT query from hrm_platform_timesheets table filtered by status='submitted' where the associated employee belongs to the current organization. Returns an integer representing the count of pending timesheets.

budgetHighUtilizationProjects.description:
Projects with budget utilization over 80%.

This metric identifies projects where the actual logged hours have consumed 80% or more of the allocated budget hours. Each entry includes project details such as id, name, budget hours, actual hours, and utilization percentage. Helps managers identify projects at risk of budget overruns.
budgetHighUtilizationProjects.x-autobe-specification: Join query between hrm_platform_projects and hrm_platform_timelogs filtered by organization_id from session. Calculate actual hours as SUM(duration_minutes)/60 per project. Filter projects where (actual_hours/budget_hours) >= 0.80. Include project id, name, budget hours, actual hours, and utilization percentage. Returns an array of IHrmPlatformHighUtilizationProjectSummary.

topEmployeesByHours.description:
Top 5 employees ranked by hours worked this week.

This metric provides a performance ranking of employees based on total hours logged within the current calendar week. Includes employee details such as id, name, department, position, and total hours. Results are ordered by total hours in descending order, limited to the top 5 employees.
topEmployeesByHours.x-autobe-specification: Join query between hrm_platform_employees and hrm_platform_timelogs filtered by current week date range and organization_id from session. Group by employee and sum duration_minutes. Order by total hours descending, limited to 5 results. Include employee id, name, department, position, and total hours. Returns an array of IHrmPlatformOrganizationDashboard.ITopEmployeeByHour.

IHrmPlatformOrganizationDashboard.description:
Aggregated organizational dashboard metrics providing an at-a-glance statistical overview of the current organization context.

This dashboard consolidates key operational KPIs including workforce statistics, time tracking summaries, budget utilization alerts, and performance rankings. All metrics are strictly scoped to the organization associated with the authenticated member's active session, ensuring multi-tenancy data isolation. No parameters are required as the organization context is automatically resolved from the session.
IHrmPlatformOrganizationDashboard.x-autobe-specification:
Computed aggregation from multiple JOIN queries scoped to organization_id from active session context:

1. activeEmployeesCount: COUNT from hrm_platform_employees WHERE status='active' and organization_id matches session
2. totalHoursThisWeek: SUM(duration_minutes)/60 from hrm_platform_timelogs where date is current week (Mon-Sun) and organization_id from session via employee relationship
3. pendingTimesheetsCount: COUNT from hrm_platform_timesheets WHERE status='submitted' and employee belongs to current organization
4. budgetHighUtilizationProjects: JOIN hrm_platform_projects with hrm_platform_timelogs, calculate actual_hours=SUM(duration_minutes)/60, include projects where (actual_hours/budget_hours)>=0.80
5. topEmployeesByHours: JOIN hrm_platform_employees with hrm_platform_timelogs for current week, GROUP BY employee, ORDER BY total_hours DESC, LIMIT 5

All queries MUST enforce organization_id filtering from session for multi-tenancy isolation.

employee_id.description:
UUID identifier of the employee who performed the tracked work.

Uniquely identifies the workforce member within their organization. Used to group and aggregate all time entries belonging to this employee for the specified project.
employee_id.x-autobe-specification: Computed field from GROUP BY hrm_platform_timelogs.hrm_platform_employee_id → hrm_platform_employees.id. The employee UUID that identifies the workforce member who performed the logged work. Used as the grouping key for per-employee aggregation.

employee_name.description:
Display name of the employee shown in user interface.

Retrieved from the employee's linked member profile (hrm_platform_members.display_name). Provides human-readable identification for reporting and dashboard displays.
employee_name.x-autobe-specification: Computed field from JOIN chain: hrm_platform_timelogs → hrm_platform_employees (via hrm_platform_employee_id → hrm_platform_employee_id). Then JOIN to hrm_platform_members via hrm_platform_member_id. Result maps to hrm_platform_members.display_name. Returns the display name shown in UI for identification purposes.

total_minutes.description:
Total minutes of tracked work logged by this employee on the specified project.

Aggregated from all active (non-deleted) timelog records. Represents cumulative work duration measured in minutes, used for budget utilization calculations and work distribution analysis.
total_minutes.x-autobe-specification: Computed via SUM(hrm_platform_timelogs.duration_minutes) filtered by projectId and deleted_at IS NULL. Aggregates duration_minutes into a cumulative integer total for payroll and budget tracking.

timelog_count.description:
Number of individual timelog entries recorded by this employee for the specified project.

Counts active (non-deleted) time tracking records. Provides insight into work session frequency and logging patterns for this employee-project combination.
timelog_count.x-autobe-specification: Computed via COUNT(*) from hrm_platform_timelogs filtered by: hrm_platform_timelogs.hrm_platform_project_id = projectId AND hrm_platform_timelogs.deleted_at IS NULL AND hrm_platform_timelogs.hrm_platform_employee_id = employee_id. Counts the number of individual timelog entries for this employee on this project. Returns 0 when no timelogs exist.

IHrmPlatformProjectTimeReport.description:
Per-employee time contribution summary for a specific project, showing each employee's total logged minutes and timelog count.

Aggregates time tracking data from active (non-deleted) timelogs associated with the specified project. Joins with employee and member records to provide human-readable employee identification alongside quantitative time metrics. Results are sorted by total minutes in descending order to surface highest contributors first.
IHrmPlatformProjectTimeReport.x-autobe-specification: Per-employee time contribution aggregation from hrm_platform_timelogs JOIN hrm_platform_employees (via hrm_platform_employee_id) JOIN hrm_platform_members (via hrm_platform_member_id). GROUP BY hrm_platform_employee_id. Filters: hrm_platform_project_id = projectId AND hrm_platform_timelogs.deleted_at IS NULL. Sorted by total_minutes descending. Edge case: empty array if no timelogs exist for the project.

id.description:
UUID identifier for the task record.

Globally unique identifier generated upon task creation. Used to reference the task in API operations, task history tracking, and timelog associations.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_platform_tasks.id. UUID primary key, auto-generated on insert.

title.description:
Core work description identifying the task.

Required text field summarizing what work needs to be done. Serves as the primary display text in task lists, project boards, and assignment notifications.
title.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_platform_tasks.title. String, NOT NULL.

description.description:
Extended context and acceptance criteria for the task.

description.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_platform_tasks.description. String, nullable. Returns null when no extended context has been provided.

status.description:
Current lifecycle position of the task.

Tracks progress through the task workflow with four allowed states: open (newly created), in-progress (actively being worked on), completed (work finished), and closed (archived). Status transitions follow a validated forward progression, and each change is recorded in the task history audit trail.
status.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_platform_tasks.status. String NOT NULL. Allowed values: open, in-progress, completed, closed. Default: open.

priority.description:
Urgency level indicating how quickly the task should be addressed.

Determines task ordering and sorting in project views. Allowed values are low, medium, high, and urgent. Defaults to medium at creation.
priority.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_platform_tasks.priority. String NOT NULL. Allowed values: low, medium, high, urgent. Default: medium.

estimatedHours.description:
Estimated work duration in hours for capacity planning.

Optional numeric value representing the expected effort required to complete the task. Used for project budget tracking, workload distribution analysis, and progress forecasting. Null when no estimate has been set.
estimatedHours.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_platform_tasks.estimated_hours. Float (DoublePrecision), nullable. Mapped to camelCase property name. Returns null when no estimate has been provided.

dueAt.description:
Deadline date and time when the task should be completed.

Optional timestamp indicating when the work item is due. Used for deadline tracking, overdue task identification, and timeline visualization in project calendars. Null when no specific deadline has been assigned.
dueAt.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_platform_tasks.due_at. DateTime (Timestamptz), nullable. Mapped to camelCase property name. Returns null when no deadline has been set.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp when the task was first created.

Immutable server-generated timestamp recorded in ISO 8601 format. Used for chronological sorting, audit trail purposes, and determining task age.
createdAt.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_platform_tasks.created_at. DateTime NOT NULL, auto-generated on insert. Mapped to camelCase property name.

Timestamp of the most recent modification to the task.

Mutable server-generated timestamp updated whenever any task attribute changes, including status transitions, title edits, priority adjustments, or assignment changes.
updatedAt.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_platform_tasks.updated_at. DateTime NOT NULL, auto-updated on any row modification. Mapped to camelCase property name.

deletedAt.description:
Soft-delete timestamp indicating task deactivation.

Nullable field that is null for active tasks. When a task is soft-deleted, this field is set to the current timestamp. Soft-deleted tasks are excluded from active listings and reports but retain their full record for audit trail preservation.
deletedAt.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_platform_tasks.deleted_at. DateTime nullable. Mapped to camelCase property name. Null for active tasks; populated with timestamp when soft-deleted.

project.description:
The project that owns and scopes this task.

Tasks are always associated with exactly one parent project, which provides organizational context and data isolation. The project summary includes name, color code, status, budget, and timeline information.
project.x-autobe-specification: BELONGS-TO relation transformed from hrm_platform_project_id FK. JOIN hrm_platform_projects on id. Returns IHrmPlatformProject.ISummary. NOT NULL — tasks always belong to exactly one project.

assignedEmployee.description:
The employee responsible for completing this task.

Optional reference to the project employee assigned to execute the work item. Assigned employees must be active project members. When null, the task is unassigned and available for work. Provides employee summary including member profile, role, department, and employment details.
assignedEmployee.x-autobe-specification: BELONGS-TO relation transformed from hrm_platform_employee_id FK. JOIN hrm_platform_employees on id. Returns IHrmPlatformEmployee.ISummary. Nullable — null when task is unassigned (hrm_platform_employee_id IS NULL).

parentTask.description:
Parent task reference for subtask nesting hierarchy.

Optional self-referential link enabling one-level subtask nesting. When present, this task is a subtask of the referenced parent task, which must belong to the same project. The parent task cannot itself have a parent (enforcing single-level nesting only). When null, this is a top-level task.
parentTask.x-autobe-specification: BELONGS-TO self-referential relation transformed from parent_id FK. JOIN hrm_platform_tasks on id recursively. Returns IHrmPlatformTask.ISummary. Nullable — null when task is not a subtask (parent_id IS NULL). One-level nesting enforced: parent tasks cannot have their own parent.

IHrmPlatformTask.description:
Full task entity representing a discrete work item within a project.

Tasks progress through a lifecycle of statuses: open, in-progress, completed, or closed. Each task has a priority level (low, medium, high, urgent), optional estimated hours for capacity planning, and an optional due date. Tasks can be assigned to a project employee and support one-level subtask nesting for hierarchical work decomposition.

The owning project is always included as a summary reference. Timestamps track creation and modification. Soft-deleted tasks retain their record with the deletedAt field populated for audit trail preservation.
IHrmPlatformTask.x-autobe-specification:
Direct mapping from hrm_platform_tasks table with FK-to-$ref transformation for all belongs-to relations.

Direct columns mapped to DTO properties:
- id → id (UUID PK)
- title → title (String NOT NULL)
- description → description (String nullable)
- status → status (String NOT NULL: open, in-progress, completed, closed)
- priority → priority (String NOT NULL: low, medium, high, urgent)
- estimated_hours → estimatedHours (Float nullable, mapped via camelCase)
- due_at → dueAt (DateTime nullable, mapped via camelCase)
- created_at → createdAt (DateTime NOT NULL, mapped via camelCase)
- updated_at → updatedAt (DateTime NOT NULL, mapped via camelCase)
- deleted_at → deletedAt (DateTime nullable, mapped via camelCase)

BELONGS-TO relations transformed from FK scalars to $ref objects:
- project: REQUIRED $ref to IHrmPlatformProject.ISummary via hrm_platform_project_id (JOIN hrm_platform_projects on id)
- assignedEmployee: OPTIONAL $ref to IHrmPlatformEmployee.ISummary via hrm_platform_employee_id (JOIN hrm_platform_employees on id, null if unassigned)
- parentTask: OPTIONAL $ref to IHrmPlatformTask.ISummary via parent_id (self-referential JOIN hrm_platform_tasks on id, null if not a subtask)

Excluded relations (HAS-MANY):
- subtasks — recursive composition, accessed via separate API
- timelogs — aggregation relation for time tracking, accessed via dedicated timelog endpoints
- hrmPlatformTimers — aggregation relation for active tracking sessions, accessed via dedicated timer endpoints
- histories — aggregation relation for task status change audit trail, accessed via dedicated task history endpoints

All column-to-DTO property mappings follow camelCase convention. FK columns are excluded as they are exposed through their corresponding relation objects.

employee.description:
The workforce member who recorded work time against this project.

Identifies the individual contributor associated with the aggregated hours and timelog count for the project.
employee.x-autobe-specification: Computed relation from hrm_platform_timelogs. The aggregation groups by the hrm_platform_employee_id column. Resolves to IHrmPlatformEmployee.ISummary by joining hrm_platform_employees.id with hrm_platform_employee_id.

hours.description:
Total hours logged by the employee against the project.

Calculated by summing all non-deleted timelog durations (stored in minutes) and dividing by 60 to convert minutes to hours. This aggregate metric represents the total actual work effort recorded by this specific employee for the project.
hours.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation from hrm_platform_timelogs. hours = SUM(timelogs.duration_minutes) / 60.0 for all non-deleted timelogs where hrm_platform_project_id matches the target project and timelogs.hrm_platform_employee_id matches the employee and timelogs.deleted_at IS NULL. Returns a float (number) representing total hours.

timelog_count.description:
The number of individual timelog entries created by this employee for the project.

Represents the count of discrete time tracking sessions (excluding soft-deleted records). This metric helps distinguish between one continuous work session and multiple shorter tracking events by the same employee against the same project.
timelog_count.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation from hrm_platform_timelogs. timelog_count = COUNT(*) where hrm_platform_project_id matches the target project, hrm_platform_employee_id matches the employee, and deleted_at IS NULL. Returns an integer with minimum 0.

IHrmPlatformProjectBudgetReport.IEmploye.description:
Per-employee time contribution record showing an individual workforce member's total hours logged against a project and the count of discrete timelog entries they created.

Used primarily in project budget utilization and time tracking reports. It groups all recorded work effort for a single project, segmenting the data by the employee who performed the work. The `employee` field identifies the contributor, `hours` provides the aggregated duration, and `timelog_count` indicates how many separate time-sessions were logged.

This breakdown supports analytical views for managers to see how project budgets are distributed across individual team members.
IHrmPlatformProjectBudgetReport.IEmploye.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation from hrm_platform_timelogs grouped by hrm_platform_employee_id. hours = SUM(duration_minutes) / 60.0 for non-deleted timelogs matching the target project. timelog_count = COUNT(*) of timelogs per employee. employee references IHrmPlatformEmployee.ISummary via join to hrm_platform_employees. Filter: timelogs.deleted_at IS NULL and hrm_platform_project_id matches target project.

id.description: Unique identifier for the activity log detail record.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_platform_activity_log_details.id. UUID primary key auto-generated by the database.

key.description:
Attribute name identifying the type of metadata stored in this detail record.

Examples include 'oldStatus' and 'newStatus' for task status changes, 'rejectionReason' for rejected timesheets, 'oldRoleId' and 'newRoleId' for role reassignments.
key.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_platform_activity_log_details.key. Attribute name identifying the metadata type. Unique within the parent activity log alongside hrm_platform_activity_log_id.

value.description:
String-encoded value of the metadata attribute.

All detail values are stored as strings to maintain uniformity across different action types. Values may represent status labels, reason texts, identifiers, or other action-specific data for audit purposes.
value.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_platform_activity_log_details.value. String-encoded metadata value stored uniformly across action types.

created_at.description: Timestamp when this detail entry was created by the system. Provides temporal context for when the metadata was attached to the log.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_platform_activity_log_details.created_at. ISO 8601 timestamp set automatically when the detail entry is created alongside its parent activity log.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this detail entry was last modified.

Updated whenever the detail value is amended. Activity logs are generally immutable but allow detail corrections for audit accuracy during the initial recording window.
updated_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_platform_activity_log_details.updated_at. ISO 8601 timestamp updated whenever the detail value is amended.

IHrmPlatformActivityLogDetail.description:
Key-value detail record providing audit context for a specific governance action.

Activity log details decompose polymorphic action metadata into atomic, structured key-value pairs to maintain strict 1NF compliance. Each detail captures exactly one attribute relevant to the logged event, such as status transitions (oldStatus, newStatus), rejection reasons (rejectionReason), or role reassignment history (oldRoleId, newRoleId).

Detail records are always accessed as part of their parent activity log entry and serve as the immutable audit trail metadata.
IHrmPlatformActivityLogDetail.x-autobe-specification: Direct mappings from hrm_platform_activity_log_details. All columns (id, key, value, created_at, updated_at) are mapped directly. Excluded: hrm_platform_activity_log_id (parent foreign key not exposed in DTO as detail records are always accessed through their parent activity log via HAS-MANY composition), activityLog (reverse belongs-to relation excluded as this DTO serves as a composed element within activity log responses).

id.description:
The unique identifier of the project.

Used to reference the project in subsequent API calls for retrieving full details, managing members, or viewing tasks and timelogs associated with the project.
id.x-autobe-specification: Derived from hrm_platform_projects.id (UUID primary key). This aggregation joins hrm_platform_projects.id to uniquely identify the project and enable navigation to full details.

name.description:
The name of the project.

Identifies the project in the budget alert list and helps managers quickly recognize which projects are at risk of exceeding their allocated time budgets.
name.x-autobe-specification: Derived from hrm_platform_projects.name. Required non-nullable field that identifies the project in list displays and reports.

budgetHours.description:
The planned budget hours for the project.

Represents the total estimated hours for project work. Only projects with a defined non-null budget appear in this high-utilization list, as they are the only ones that can be measured against actual time consumption.
budgetHours.x-autobe-specification: Derived from hrm_platform_projects.budget (Float/DoublePrecision). Only projects with non-null budget values are included in high-utilization reports. The non-null DTO constraint is enforced by query filter excluding null budget projects.

actualHours.description:
The total actual hours logged against the project by all employees.

Computed by summing the duration_minutes of all non-deleted timelogs for this project and converting to hours. This value is compared against budgetHours to determine utilization percentage.
actualHours.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation from hrm_platform_timelogs: SUM(duration_minutes) / 60, grouped by project_id. Only non-soft-deleted timelogs (deleted_at IS NULL) are included in the summation. Results in total hours (not minutes) for display consistency with budgetHours.

utilizationPercentage.description:
The percentage of budget hours consumed by actual logged time.

Calculated as (actualHours / budgetHours) multiplied by 100. Only projects at or above 80 percent budget utilization appear in this list, acting as a critical indicator for project managers to track potentially at-risk projects.
utilizationPercentage.x-autobe-specification: Computed value: (actualHours / budgetHours) * 100. Only projects where utilizationPercentage >= 80.0 are included in this DTO's result set. The minimum: 80 JSON Schema constraint documents this filtering threshold.

IHrmPlatformHighUtilizationProjectSummar.description:
Summary of a project with budget utilization at or above 80%, showing budget hours, actual hours logged, and utilization percentage.

This type appears in the organization dashboard's budget alert list, helping managers identify projects at risk of exceeding their allocated time budgets. Each entry includes the project identifier, planned budget hours, actual hours consumed from employee timelogs, and the computed utilization percentage.

Used exclusively in response DTOs — never appears in request bodies or query parameters.
IHrmPlatformHighUtilizationProjectSummar.x-autobe-specification:
Computed aggregation from JOIN hrm_platform_projects with hrm_platform_timelogs scoped to organization_id from active session context:
    - id: hrm_platform_projects.id (UUID primary key)
    - name: hrm_platform_projects.name (project identification)
    - budgetHours: hrm_platform_projects.budget (Float/DoublePrecision). Only non-null budgets qualify for filtering.
    - actualHours: SUM(duration_minutes) / 60 from hrm_platform_timelogs GROUP BY project_id, excluding soft-deleted timelogs (deleted_at IS NULL).
    - utilizationPercentage: (actualHours / budgetHours) * 100, computed only when >= 80.0.
    
    Multi-tenancy: All queries MUST be filtered by organization_id matching the authenticated member's active session context.

billable.description:
Determines if this breakdown represents billable or non-billable time.

Returns true for client chargeable hours and false for internal organizational work. Aggregates all time entries for the project that match this exact billability classification.
billable.x-autobe-specification: Derived from hrm_platform_timelogs.billable grouping logic. The Boolean value being grouped to separate client chargeable work (true) from internal organizational work (false).

total_hours.description:
Total hours logged in this billability category.

Represents the aggregated duration of time entries that fall into either the billable or non-billable category. Computed by summing raw duration minutes and dividing by 60.0, rounded to represent decimal hours for financial reporting.
total_hours.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation. Calculates SUM(hrm_platform_timelogs.duration_minutes) / 60.0 for timelogs matching the grouped billable flag and the referencing project where deleted_at IS NULL. If no timelogs exist for this billable category, total_hours will be 0.

timelog_count.description:
The number of individual timelog entries within this billability category.

Counts the exact number of time tracking records classified as either billable or non-billable, filtered by the project scope and excluding soft-deleted entries.
timelog_count.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation. Calculates COUNT(*) of hrm_platform_timelogs matching the grouped billable flag and the referencing project where deleted_at IS NULL. If no timelogs exist for this billable category, timelog_count will be 0.

IHrmPlatformProjectBudgetReport.IBillabl.description:
Billable time breakdown showing total hours and timelog count.

Separates project time into client chargeable (billable=true) versus internal organizational (billable=false) work. Each breakdown object represents one billability classification with the aggregated total hours logged and the number of individual time entries that fall into that category. Returns exactly two objects per budget report: one for billable hours and one for non-billable hours.
IHrmPlatformProjectBudgetReport.IBillabl.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation type based on hrm_platform_timelogs. Groups time entries by billability flag. Calculates billable (the grouped Boolean value), total_hours (SUM(duration_minutes) / 60.0), and timelog_count (COUNT(*)) for timelogs belonging to the referenced project where deleted_at IS NULL. Returns exactly two breakdown objects per budget report: one with billable=true and one with billable=false. If no timelogs exist for a billable category, both total_hours and timelog_count will be 0.

position.description:
Optional job title or position name.

Human-readable position title assigned to the employee within the organization. Provides role context alongside department information. Null if no position title has been specified for this employee.
position.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_platform_employees.position column. Nullable string field storing the optional job title or position name for the employee within the organization.

department.description:
Optional department affiliation for organizational context.

References the department within which the employee is grouped. Provides department name and hierarchical parent information for organizational structure display. Null when the employee reports directly to the organization without a specific department assignment.
department.x-autobe-specification: Join from employees.hrm_platform_department_id to hrm_platform_departments.id via the department relation. Returns IHrmPlatformDepartment.ISummary with id, name, parentDepartment, and timestamps. Nullable when employee has no department assignment.

member.description:
Linked member profile for display name and contact information.

References the global user account associated with this employee. Provides the display name shown in the dashboard ranking, along with email, avatar, and phone number. Member profiles are shared across all organizational contexts.
member.x-autobe-specification: Join from employees.hrm_platform_member_id to hrm_platform_members.id via the member relation. Returns IHrmPlatformMember.ISummary containing display_name, email, avatar_image, and phone_number for identification and display purposes.

totalHours.description:
Total hours logged during the current calendar week.

Aggregated sum of all timelog durations for this employee within the current week (Monday through Sunday). Duration values are summed in minutes and converted to hours (divided by 60). Only active, non-deleted timelogs are counted. Primary ranking metric for the top employees visualization on the organization dashboard.
totalHours.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation field. Calculated as SUM(timelogs.duration_minutes) / 60.0 for all non-deleted timelogs belonging to this employee within the current calendar week (Monday through Sunday) and matching the organization_id from the authenticated session context. Only timelogs with deleted_at IS NULL are included. Result is a floating-point number representing total hours worked.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the employee.

Universally unique identifier (UUID) that represents the employee record within the organization. Serves as the grouping key for aggregating timelog hours and uniquely identifies each ranked employee in the dashboard.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_platform_employees.id. UUID primary key identifying the employee record used in the hours aggregation grouping.

IHrmPlatformOrganizationDashboard.ITopEm.description:
Top employee ranking entry showing hours worked during the current calendar week.

Each entry represents an employee ranked by total hours logged, combining employee identity (UUID), linked member profile for display name, optional department affiliation, optional position title, and the computed total hours worked. This data powers the organization dashboard's top 5 employee ranking visualization.

Used by managers to recognize high contributors and monitor workload distribution across the team.
IHrmPlatformOrganizationDashboard.ITopEm.x-autobe-specification:
Join aggregation from hrm_platform_employees with hrm_platform_timelogs, filtered by current calendar week date range and organization_id from authenticated session context. Results grouped by employee and ordered by computed total hours descending, limited to top 5.

Data source mapping:
- id from employees.id
- member from employees.hrm_platform_member_id joined to hrm_platform_members via $ref to IHrmPlatformMember.ISummary
- department from employees.hrm_platform_department_id joined to hrm_platform_departments via $ref to IHrmPlatformDepartment.ISummary (nullable - employees may lack department assignment)
- position from employees.position column (nullable)
- totalHours computed as SUM(timelogs.duration_minutes) / 60.0

Only active employees (status = 'active') with non-deleted timelogs are included.

instruction:
Generate comprehensive E2E test suites for all API endpoints of the ERP HRM & Time Tracking Platform. Cover all the following domains:

1. **Organization tests**: Create, update, delete organization (including validation that deletion fails when pending timesheets exist or active contracts exist)
2. **User Account tests**: Signup, login, change password, delete account, switch organization context
3. **User Profile tests**: Get/update profile
4. **Roles & Permissions tests**: List roles, create/update/delete custom roles, validate built-in roles cannot be deleted, validate role deletion fails when assigned to employees
5. **Department tests**: CRUD departments, validate parent-child nesting (one level), validate employee department sets to null on department delete
6. **Employee Management tests**: 
   - Invite employee (existing user vs new email/pending invitation)
   - List employees with pagination, filtering (department, employment type, status), and search by name
   - Deactivate/reactivate employee (verify deactivated employees cannot log time)
   - Change employee role
7. **Contract tests**: 
   - Create contract (verify previous active contract auto-closes)
   - Update active contract only (past contracts immutable)
   - List contracts
8. **Project tests**: 
   - CRUD projects
   - Archive/complete project (verify archived projects reject new timelogs)
   - Delete project only when no timelogs exist
   - Manage project members (assign/remove, member vs project-lead)
9. **Task tests**: 
   - CRUD tasks with subtask nesting (one level)
   - Task history tracking (status changes recorded with timestamp, old/new status, user)
   - Filter by status, priority, assigned employee; sort by due date, priority, created at
   - Verify only project members can view tasks in their projects
10. **Timelog tests**: 
    - Create/update/delete timelogs for own employee
    - Verify timelogs cannot be created for archived/completed projects
    - Verify timelogs in approved timesheets cannot be edited/deleted
    - Verify submitted timesheet timelogs cannot be deleted
    - time:manage permission can manage any employee's timelogs
    - Pagination and filtering (date range, project, task, billable)
11. **Timesheet tests**: 
    - Create draft (auto-include weekly timelogs)
    - Add/remove timelogs from draft
    - Submit timesheet (validation: must have timelogs, no duplicate week submitted/approved)
    - Approve timesheet (verify timelogs locked)
    - Reject timesheet with reason (returns to draft, employee can resubmit)
    - Pagination and filtering (status, date range)
12. **Timer tests**: 
    - Start timer (verify only one active timer per employee)
    - Stop timer (creates timelog with duration rounded to nearest minute)
    - Discard timer (no timelog created)
    - Update running timer (description, project, task)
    - Get active timer
13. **Reports tests**: 
    - Time report (grouped by employee/project/task, billable/non-billable breakdown)
    - Project budget report (budget vs actual, percentage consumed)
    - Weekly summary report (week-by-week with hours, timelog count, employee count)
14. **Activity Log tests**: 
    - Verify activity logs created for: employee invite/deactivate/reactivate, contract CRUD, project CRUD, task status change, timesheet submit/approve/reject, role assignment
    - Pagination and filtering (action type, user, date range)
15. **Dashboard tests**: 
    - Personal dashboard: hours today/week, active timer status, recent timelogs, pending timesheet, assigned tasks
    - Organization dashboard: active employees count, total hours this week, pending timesheets, projects over 80% budget, top 5 employees

16. **Data Isolation tests**: 
    - Verify users cannot access data from other organizations
    - Verify users with multiple organizations only see data for current context
    - Verify employee records in other orgs are marked deactivated when user account deleted

17. **Permission tests**: 
    - Verify all permission checks work correctly (org:manage, employee:manage, employee:view, project:manage, project:view, time:manage, time:approve, time:view_all, report:view)
    - Verify unauthorized access returns 403

Use test scenarios that verify both happy paths and error cases. Structure tests with proper setup and teardown using factories or seed data. Ensure all API endpoints are covered with at least one test each.

import { IEntity } from "@ORGANIZATION/PROJECT-api/lib/structures/IEntity";
import { IHrmPlatformOrganization } from "@ORGANIZATION/PROJECT-api/lib/structures/IHrmPlatformOrganization";
import { DeepPartial } from "@ORGANIZATION/PROJECT-api/lib/typings/DeepPartial";
import { ArrayUtil, RandomGenerator } from "@nestia/e2e";
import { randint } from "tstl";
import typia, { tags } from "typia";

/**
 * Prepare random HRM platform organization creation data for E2E testing.
 *
 * Generates a complete IHrmPlatformOrganization.ICreate with randomized values
 * for organization name, description, logo URI, currency, timezone, and fiscal
 * year start month. The name is generated as a human-readable identifier, while
 * currency and timezone are picked from realistic options.
 *
 * All fields can be partially overridden via the `input` parameter for
 * targeted test scenarios.
 */
export function prepare_random_hrm_platform_organization(
  input?: DeepPartial<IHrmPlatformOrganization.ICreate> | undefined,
): IHrmPlatformOrganization.ICreate {
  return {
    name: input?.name ?? RandomGenerator.name(2),
    description:
      input?.description ?? RandomGenerator.paragraph({ sentences: 2 }),
    logo_uri:
      input?.logo_uri ??
      `https://example.com/logos/${RandomGenerator.alphaNumeric(8)}.png`,
    currency:
      input?.currency ??
      RandomGenerator.pick([
        "USD",
        "EUR",
        "KRW",
        "GBP",
        "JPY",
        "CAD",
        "AUD",
      ] as const),
    timezone:
      input?.timezone ??
      RandomGenerator.pick([
        "America/New_York",
        "America/Chicago",
        "America/Los_Angeles",
        "Europe/London",
        "Europe/Paris",
        "Asia/Seoul",
        "Asia/Tokyo",
        "Australia/Sydney",
      ] as const),
    fiscal_start_month:
      input?.fiscal_start_month ??
      typia.random<
        number & tags.Type<"int32"> & tags.Minimum<1> & tags.Maximum<12>
      >(),
  };
}

scenario.draft:
Test guest join operation for a brand new visitor accessing public entry points.

**Test Steps**:
1. Call POST /hrmPlatform/auth/guest/join with device_fingerprint="visitor-device-001", href="https://app.example.com/signup"
2. Verify response IAuthorized returns guest id (valid UUID) and token object with access (JWT), refresh, expired_at (valid ISO timestamp), refreshable_until
3. Call POST /hrmPlatform/auth/guest/join with SAME device_fingerprint but different href
4. Verify the guest id is identical to the first call (proving find-or-create behavior)
5. Verify the second call returns new tokens (proving session renewal)

**Business Validation**:
- First call creates a new anonymous visitor session
- Second call with same device fingerprint correctly reuses existing guest profile
- Guest identity continuity across public page visits
- Device fingerprint is the sole identity key for anonymous visitors

dependencies.purpose:
Essential authentication prerequisite:
This join operation (post /hrmPlatform/auth/guest/join) must be executed before any operations requiring 'guest' actor authorization.
It establishes the necessary user account and authentication context for the 'guest' actor, enabling subsequent API calls that depend on this specific authorization level.
Without this join operation, the main scenario endpoint and its dependencies will fail due to insufficient authentication credentials.

functions.name: test_api_guest_initial_session_creation

scenario.draft:
Test guest join operation when a returning visitor uses the same device fingerprint.

**Test Steps**:
1. First call POST /hrmPlatform/auth/guest/join with device_fingerprint="persistent-device-abc", href="https://app.example.com/signup"
2. Capture guest id from first response
3. Second call POST /hrmPlatform/auth/guest/join with SAME device_fingerprint
4. Verify the guest id from the second call equals the guest id from the first call (identical IDs)
5. Verify the second call returns new tokens (different access/refresh, new expired_at/refreshable_until - fresh session)

**Business Validation**:
- Find-or-create: same device_fingerprint reuses existing guest profile
- Guest identity continuity across multiple public page visits
- Each join creates a fresh session with new tokens even for returning guests
- Device fingerprint is the sole identity key for anonymous visitors

dependencies.purpose:

scenario.draft: Test the primary session renewal workflow for unauthenticated guest users browsing public entry points. After establishing an initial guest session via join, capture the issued refresh token. Submit this refresh token to the refresh endpoint. Verify the response returns a renewed IAuthorized object containing: (1) a guest id matching the original session, (2) a new access token for API authentication, (3) a new refresh token for subsequent renewals, (4) an updated expired_at timestamp showing extended session validity for the access token, and (5) an updated refreshable_until timestamp indicating the new absolute session deadline. This validates the complete token rotation business workflow where anonymous visitors can continue browsing sign-up and login pages without interruption. Verify the expired_at and refreshable_until timestamps are both in the future, demonstrating successful session extension.

scenario.draft:
**Steps**:
1. Authenticate as a member.
2. Create a custom role with a unique name and specific permission keys.
3. Call GET /hrmPlatform/member/roles/{roleId} using the created role's ID.

**Validations**:
- Response returns HTTP 200 OK.
- Response body matches `IHrmPlatformRole` schema.
- `id` matches the `roleId` path parameter.
- `built_in` is `false`.
- `name` matches the name provided during role creation.
- `description` matches the provided description or is `null` if none was provided.
- `rolePermissions` is an array of `IHrmPlatformRolePermission` objects.
- `rolePermissions` length exactly matches the number of `permissionKeys` assigned during creation.
- `created_at` and `updated_at` are valid ISO 8601 date-time timestamps.

**Business Logic**:
- Custom roles are fully customizable by the organization owner.
- Role permissions are dynamically mapped to the custom role.
- Multi-tenancy isolation is enforced.
